key_insight: MOTIF improves out-of-distribution materials property prediction by using LLMs to propose chemical taxonomies rather than predict numerical properties directly.
engineering_relevance: The framework can improve prediction robustness for unfamiliar material families by selecting features that generalize across chemically meaningful groups.
method: Use LLMs to generate candidate taxonomies that partition materials into chemical environments.
Retain taxonomies that improve training-only pseudo-OOD validation, then apply invariant feature selection within each.
Combine predictions across accepted taxonomies using gated aggregation.
evidence_signal: On 2D halide perovskites, mean OOD bandgap MAE fell from 0.122 to 0.111 eV; frozen dev/test evaluation showed smaller gains, with transferability also evaluated on 3D perovskite solar cell efficiencies and Matbench structure-based splits.
watch_item: Deployment depends on whether training-only pseudo-OOD validation selects taxonomies that remain useful under the actual chemistry shift.
paper_title: MOTIF: LLM-Defined Material Taxonomies for OOD Property Prediction via Invariant Feature Selection
